topics.title: 1. Network Basics, Protocols, Topologies & Network Types
topics.theory:
- **Protocol** = set of rules for communication: **syntax** (format), **semantics** (meaning), **timing** (order/speed).
- **Topologies:** Bus (single shared cable, *multipoint*, cheap, cable fault kills all) · Star (central hub/switch, **central device = single point of failure**, easy fault isolation) · Ring (closed loop, token passing) · Mesh · Tree · Hybrid.
- **Full mesh with n nodes:** links = **n(n−1)/2**, ports per node = **n−1** (n(n−1) counts each link twice — classic trap).
- **Network types:** PAN < LAN (building) < MAN (city, connects LANs, data + voice) < WAN (country/world, satellite/microwave/leased line, *slower* than LAN). LAN technologies: Ethernet, Token Ring, FDDI. **Frame Relay / X.25 / ATM are WAN technologies.**
- **Client-server** needs a dedicated server; **peer-to-peer**: every node is both client and server, any peer can access any other.
- **Distributed computing:** many autonomous computers, each with own memory, linked by a network, present as a *single system*; supports scalability and resource sharing. Parallel computing = split one task to run simultaneously (shared memory/same machine).
- **ARPANET** = Advanced Research Projects Agency Network — forerunner of the Internet, first **packet-switched** network.
- 5 components of a network: sender, receiver, message, medium, protocol.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a type of Network topology?
qs.sol: Answer:  Singleton Network
qs.rel: Topology = physical/logical arrangement of nodes. Real ones: bus, star, ring, mesh, tree, hybrid. Bus is the only multipoint one; star's hub is a single point of failure; mesh needs n(n-1)/2 links.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is a type of network topology?

I. Star topology 

II. Bus topology 

III. Car topology
qs.sol:
A network topology defines the arrangement of various elements (links, nodes, etc.) of a computer network.

Star topology connects all devices to a central hub, while Bus topology connects all devices to a single central cable. Both are standard and widely recognized configurations in computer networking.

Car topology is not a standard term in computer networking or infrastructure design. Therefore, it is not a valid network topology.

Thus, statements I and II are correct, while statement III is incorrect.
qs.rel: Topology identification. Bus = shared backbone with terminators; star = central switch; ring = closed loop with token. Tree is a hierarchy of stars. Expect 'which topology needs most cabling' (mesh) or 'easiest fault isolation' (star).

qs.stem: _____ is a set of rules that governs how two computer systems interact.
qs.sol:
Concept: A protocol is a formal set of rules and conventions that two or more communicating systems agree to follow. It fixes the syntax (format of the data), the semantics (meaning of each field or message), and the timing/sequencing (order in which messages are exchanged), so that independently built systems can interoperate reliably.

Application: The blank in the question describes exactly this role — a defined framework that governs the format, order, and actions used when two computer systems interact. That description matches the definition of a protocol, so the correct term is Protocol. …
qs.rel: Protocol = syntax + semantics + timing. Standards bodies: ISO, IEEE, IETF, ITU-T. Examples by layer: HTTP/FTP/SMTP (application), TCP/UDP (transport), IP (network). Interface vs protocol: interface is between adjacent layers, protocol between peers.

qs.stem: How many maximum links can be created in a mesh topology network of n computers?
qs.sol:
In a full mesh topology, every single computer (or node) must be directly connected to every other computer in the network.

If you have n computers, each computer needs a connection to all the other computers, which is n - 1 links.

If you multiply the number of computers (n) by the links they each need (n - 1), you get n(n - 1).

However, a link between Computer A and Computer B is the exact same physical cable as the link between Computer B and Computer A. To avoid counting every cable twice, you have to divide the total by 2.
qs.rel: Full mesh: links n(n-1)/2, ports per node n-1, total ports n(n-1). 10 nodes -> 45 links, 9 ports each. Contrast: star n links, ring n links, bus one backbone with n drop lines.

qs.sol: Modified from the official paper: the official question was ignored because the printed conditions did not determine a unique topology. The added closed-loop condition makes ring topology unique. A ring connects peers in a loop; a bus instead uses a common backbone.
qs.rel: Ring topology: each node has exactly two neighbours, data circulates in one direction (token passing). Contrast bus (shared backbone, collisions) and star (central node). FDDI uses a dual ring; a single break stops a simple ring.

qs.stem: What is the full form of ARPANET, which was an experimental computer network that was the forerunner of the Internet?
qs.sol: ARPANET stands for Advanced Research Projects Agency Network. It was the experimental network that became a forerunner of the Internet.
qs.rel: ARPANET (1969, US DoD) pioneered packet switching and moved to TCP/IP on 1 Jan 1983. Successors: NSFNET (1986), then the commercial Internet. WWW (Tim Berners-Lee, CERN) is an application on the Internet, not the Internet itself.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a multipoint networking topology?
qs.sol:
In a bus topology multiple devices share one communication medium, making the connection multipoint.

Bus lets multiple nodes share the same link.
qs.rel: Multipoint (multidrop) = link shared by more than two devices: bus. Star, mesh and ring are built from point-to-point links. Bus uses terminators to stop signal reflection and has collisions, handled by CSMA/CD.

qs.stem:
Which statements are true about wide area network?
 I. Covers wide geographical area
 II. Communication takes place by way of satellites, microwaves
 III. Relatively faster than local area network
qs.sol:
Answer: I and II are true; III is false.

I. Covers wide geographical area — True. WANs connect devices across cities, countries, or continents.

II. Communication takes place by way of satellites, microwaves — True. WAN links commonly use satellite, microwave, fiber-optic, and leased-line technologies for long-distance communication.

III. Relatively faster than local area network — False. LANs typically offer higher bandwidth and lower latency because they operate over shorter distances and use faster media, so WANs are usually slower than LANs. …
qs.rel: WAN = country/world scale, uses leased lines, satellites, microwave, packet networks (X.25, Frame Relay, ATM). Hence satellite/microwave are WAN features. MAN covers a city; WAN is not usually owned by one organisation; Internet is the largest WAN.

qs.stem:
Which statements are true about Local Area Network (LAN)?
 I. Communication takes place by way of satellites, microwave
 II. Faster than wide area network
 III. Covers limited area
qs.sol:
Answer: Statements II and III are true; statement I is false.

Statement I: "Communication takes place by way of satellites, microwave." — False. Local Area Networks typically use wired technologies like Ethernet or short‑range wireless technologies like Wi‑Fi. Satellites and long‑range microwave links are used for wide‑area communication, not for typical LANs.

Statement II: "Faster than wide area network." — True. LANs generally offer higher bandwidth and lower latency than WANs because they span a small, local area and use high‑speed links.

Statement III: "Covers limited area." — True. By definition, a LAN covers a limited geographic area such as a home, office, or building. …
qs.rel: LAN: single building/campus, privately owned, high speed, low error, uses Ethernet/Wi-Fi/Token Ring/FDDI. Satellite/microwave links and wide coverage are WAN traits. Compare range: PAN (m) < LAN < CAN < MAN < WAN.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? 

I. Metropolitan area network is a collection of Local area network .

II. Metropolitan area network support both data and voices transmission.
qs.sol: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) connects multiple Local Area Networks (LANs) within a specific geographic area like a city, making Statement I correct. Additionally, MAN infrastructure supports both data and voice transmission, validating Statement II. Therefore, both statements are correct.
qs.rel: MAN = collection of LANs spanning a city, carries data and voice (cable TV network, DQDB). Typical MAN technologies: FDDI, ATM, SMDS. WAN extends further; contrast PAN/LAN scale and ownership.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements about distributed computing is FALSE?

opts.B: Each computer system in distributed computing has its own memory.
opts.C: It does not allow for scalability and resource sharing.
opts.D: The computer systems connect with one another via a network.

qs.sol: The FALSE statement is Option C. It claims distributed computing does not allow scalability, which is incorrect as scalability is a core benefit.
qs.rel: Distributed system = autonomous computers appearing as one coherent system; transparency (access, location, replication, failure). It supports scalability and fault tolerance. Contrast parallel computing (tightly coupled, shared memory) and client-server.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a LAN technology?
qs.sol:
Concept

Network technologies are classified by the geographic scope and service they are designed to support. A LAN links devices within a limited site; a WAN service interconnects networks or sites over wider distances, often through a carrier.

Application

Frame Relay operates through provider-managed packet-switched virtual circuits and was designed to connect separated sites; its operating scope is therefore wide-area networking.

Contrast

Fiber Distributed Data Interface (FDDI) uses dual token rings and 100 Mbit/s fiber links for local or campus backbones.

Token Ring uses a circulating token to control transmission on a logical ring within a local network. …
qs.rel: Frame Relay, X.25, ATM, ISDN, leased lines are WAN technologies. LAN technologies: Ethernet 802.3, Token Ring 802.5, Token Bus 802.4, FDDI, Wi-Fi 802.11. Frame Relay is a virtual-circuit packet service.

qs.stem:
The main aim of which of the following is to make a network work as a single computer? 

(i) Distributed computing 
(ii) Parallel computing
qs.sol:
Concept

Distributed computing coordinates autonomous computers connected by a network so that communication, resource sharing, and services can be presented as one coherent system. Parallel computing divides a computation into simultaneous tasks to reduce execution time; it may use processors within one machine and does not by itself define a network-wide single-system view.

Application

Distributed computing coordinates networked machines and presents their resources through a coherent system view. Parallel computing decomposes a workload for simultaneous execution to reduce elapsed time. …
qs.rel: Distributed computing hides the network so many machines act as a single computer (transparency). Middleware sits between OS and applications. Distinguish it from a computer network, which only shares resources without a unified view.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are not true about star topology?
 I. Failure of the central computer shuts down the entire network
 II. Connection of additional computers increases the communication time
qs.sol: Concept: In a star topology every node connects to the network through a single central connecting device (a hub or switch) over an independent, dedicated point-to-point link — this is the standard model assumed for star topology in networking exams. Two structural consequences follow from this design: (a) the central device sits on every path between two nodes, so it is the network's single point of failure, and (b) each link's own transmission time depends primarily on that link and the central device's forwarding capacity, not on the sheer count of other nodes attached — merely attaching another device does not, by itself, add traffic onto an existing link. …
qs.rel: Star topology: failure of one node/cable affects only that node, but failure of the central hub/switch brings the whole network down. Easy to add nodes and isolate faults; needs n cables. Hub-based star shares a collision domain; switch-based does not.

qs.stem: In __________ type of distributed systems, the nodes play an important role in this system and the task is evenly distributed among the nodes.
qs.sol: The correct answer is Option C, peer-to-peer system. In a peer-to-peer (P2P) distributed architecture, every node functions as both a client and a server. Unlike traditional models where specific machines handle requests for others, P2P systems rely on the collective resources of all participating nodes. This means that tasks and data are distributed evenly across the network, with each node playing an equally important role in processing requests and sharing resources. This contrasts sharply with a file server system (Option B), where a central server manages files and clients merely request them, creating an imbalance in roles. …
qs.rel: Peer-to-peer: every node is both client and server, no central server, cheap, hard to secure and administer centrally. Examples BitTorrent, early Napster (hybrid). Contrast client-server: centralised control, dedicated server, better security.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding Peer-to-Peer Network Architecture? I. Any peer can access any other peer on the network for sharing and retrieving data II. Needs a dedicated server to provide various services to client
qs.sol: Peers can act as both clients and resource providers, so one peer can share with another. A dedicated service server is characteristic of client–server architecture, not a requirement of peer-to-peer networking. Therefore statement I alone is correct.
qs.rel: P2P: any peer can request and provide services, no dedicated server. Weaknesses: poor central security, backup and administration. Strength: no single point of failure and capacity scales with peers. Contrast with client-server scalability limits.

qs.stem: MAN stands for :
qs.sol:
MAN stands for Metropolitan Area Network.

It is a network that spans a metropolitan area, generally larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN.

qs.stem: Which one of the following is not a network topology?
qs.sol:
Network Topology Analysis

Network topology refers to the arrangement of various elements (links, nodes, etc.) of a computer network. Common topologies include Ring, Bus, and Star.

Ring Topology: Devices are connected in a closed loop where data travels in one direction.

Bus Topology: All devices are connected to a single central cable known as the backbone.

Star Topology: All devices are connected to a central hub or switch.

A Stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In First Out (LIFO) principle. It is used for managing data in memory, not for physical network connections.

Therefore, Stack is not a network topology. …

Network topologies define how devices are connected in a network. Common topologies include Star, Ring, and Mesh. In Star topology, all devices connect to a central hub. In Ring topology, devices are connected in a closed loop. In Mesh topology, each device connects to every other device. Disk is not a network topology; it refers to a storage device or data storage method, not a network arrangement. Therefore, 'Disk' is not a network topology. …
Answer:  RAM

qs.stem: Which of the following terms is used to represent "a set of rules" in computer networks ?
qs.sol: A network protocol is an agreed set of rules for formatting, transmitting, and receiving information.

qs.stem: Internet is an example of:
qs.sol: The Internet is the world’s largest Wide Area Network (WAN), connecting computers and networks across countries and continents.

qs.stem: Which one of the following is not a network topology?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol: Network topology refers to the arrangement of nodes and connections in a network. Common topologies include bus, ring, star, and mesh. Peer-to-peer is not a topology; it is a network model where devices communicate directly without a central server. In contrast, ring and bus are physical or logical layouts that define how devices are connected. Therefore, peer-to-peer is not a network topology. …

qs.stem: Which network topology requires a central controller or hub?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Step 1: In a star topology, all devices are connected to a central hub or switch. This central node manages data transmission between devices, making it essential for network operation.

Step 2: In a mesh topology, each device is directly connected to every other device. This allows peer-to-peer communication without a central controller.

Step 3: In a ring topology, devices are connected in a circular loop. Data travels around the ring, and each device acts as a repeater, eliminating the need for a central hub.

Step 4: Only the star topology requires a central controller. Therefore, the correct answer is the one indicating a central hub is needed. …

qs.stem: The topology with highest reliability is
qs.sol: A network switch connects multiple computers/devices within a network and helps in communication. Hence, it is a networking device.

qs.stem: The topology with highest reliability is

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Mesh topology is the network topology with the highest reliability. Because every node is directly connected to every other node, it provides multiple redundant, dedicated, point-to-point paths for data transmission. If one link or node fails, data can be rerouted through another path, ensuring continuous operation

Printed order: (A) star; (B) ring; (C) mesh; (D) More than one of the above; (E) None of the above.

qs.stem: Which of the following topologies gives highest reliability?
qs.sol:
In Mesh topology, each node is connected to multiple other nodes.

Failure of one link or node does not affect communication between other nodes.

Hence, it provides the highest reliability.

qs.stem: If all devices are connected to a central hub, then the topology is called:
qs.sol: Every endpoint has its own link to one central hub. That physical arrangement is a star network.

qs.stem: Which term describes the way devices are interconnected in a network?
qs.sol:
Correct Answer: Topology

The term that describes the way devices are interconnected in a network is Topology.

Network topology defines the physical or logical layout of the network. It specifies how nodes (computers, printers, servers) are connected and how data flows between them. Common types include Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh, and Tree topologies. …

qs.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of computer networks?
qs.sol:
Concept: A computer network connects devices so they can exchange data and use shared services. Its benefits depend on the system design: shared resources can reduce duplication, redundancy can sustain access after failures, and distributed work can improve throughput.

Application to the listed properties:

Resource sharing lets multiple users access common files, printers, or connections.

Reliability and availability can improve when replicated services or alternate paths keep access working after a component fails.

Performance can improve when networked machines divide work or balance traffic; this depends on adequate capacity and configuration. …

qs.stem: In which network topology are all individual nodes connected to a central connection point, such as a hub or switch?
qs.sol: In a Star Topology, all individual nodes connect directly to a central connection point such as a hub or switch. This distinguishes it from Bus Topology, where nodes share a single communication line, and Ring Topology, where nodes are connected in a closed loop. The description provided matches the definition of Star Topology.

qs.stem: _________ topology requires highest number of ports and largest amount of cabling in computer networks.
qs.sol:
In computer networks, different topologies have varying requirements for ports and cabling. Let's analyze each option:

Star Topology

In star topology, each device connects to a central hub using a dedicated cable. This requires one port per device on the hub and a separate cable for each connection. As the number of devices increases, the number of ports and cables grows significantly, making it less efficient in terms of port and cabling usage.

Ring Topology

In ring topology, devices are connected in a closed loop. Each device connects to two neighbors, using only two ports per device. …

Correct answer:  LAN  (Local Area Network)
 Why LAN is correct:
 A LAN connects computers within a limited area such as a single classroom, computer lab, school building, or office floor.

Typical LAN hardware includes switches, routers, and Ethernet cabling — exactly the networking devices and wired cables mentioned in the question.

A LAN easily supports dozens of computers in one physical location; connecting 20 computers in one lab is a standard LAN use case.

Why the other network types are not suitable:
 MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers a much larger area such as a city or large campus, so it is too large for a single school lab. …

qs.stem: Which type of wired network is commonly used to share a printer among 8 computers in an office room ?
qs.sol:
Classify networks by geographic extent.

The eight machines and shared printer are in one office room, a small local area.

A wired local area network fits that scope.

qs.stem: A network spreading in different geographical locations is known as —
qs.sol: A WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large geographical areas, such as cities, countries, or continents.

qs.stem: In networking, a set of rules that governs how data is formatted, transmitted and received between devices is called a/an:
qs.sol: In networking, a protocol is the specific set of rules that governs how data is formatted, transmitted, and received between devices. This distinguishes it from algorithms (which are calculation procedures) or topology (which refers to network layout).

qs.stem: A .......... is a set of formal operating rules, procedure or conventions that govern a given process.
qs.sol:
A protocol is a set of formal operating rules, procedures, or conventions that govern a given process. In networking, protocols define how data is transmitted and received between devices. They ensure compatibility and standard communication across different systems.

This definition aligns with the concept of a protocol, which establishes the rules for interaction. Other terms like routing or switching refer to specific actions or layers within a network architecture, rather than the governing rules themselves.

Option text corrected to the printed paper.

qs.stem: Which of the following term is used for a computer network that typically connects personal computers within a limited geographical area, usually within a single building ?
qs.sol: A local area network connects devices over a limited area such as a building or campus.

qs.stem: A company connects its offices located in different cities across the globe. This type of network is classified as a:
qs.sol: A network that connects offices across different cities and globally is classified as a Wide Area Network (WAN). While Local Area Networks (LANs) cover small areas like buildings, and Metropolitan Area Networks (MANs) cover a city, WANs are designed to span large geographic regions. Personal Area Networks (PANs) cover only an individual's immediate space.

qs.stem: A _____ is used to connect networking devices that are in a very close geographic area such as a floor of a building.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept: Networks are classified primarily by the geographic area they span, from smallest to largest:

PAN (Personal Area Network) — devices around a single person, typically a few centimetres to a few metres (e.g., a phone paired with a Bluetooth headset).

LAN (Local Area Network) — devices within one building, floor, or small campus, typically tens to a few hundred metres.

MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) — devices across a city or a large multi-building campus, several kilometres.

WAN (Wide Area Network) — devices across cities, countries, or continents, using long-haul links. …

qs.stem: What is the full form of ARPANET?

opts.A: Advancement of Research Projects Agency Network
opts.C: Add on Research Projects Agency Network

qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: the printed expansion choices use “Project” singular, while the standard ARPANET expansion uses “Projects” plural.

CONCEPT

An acronym is expanded by matching each letter to the exact words in the official name. Historical names must preserve their documented wording, including singular or plural forms.

For a full-form question, compare every word in each proposed expansion with the established name rather than relying only on the initials. …

qs.stem: ______________ is an agreement between the communicating parties on how communication is to proceed over a network.
qs.sol:
Correct Answer: Protocol / प्रोटोकॉल

A protocol is a set of rules and conventions that govern how data is transmitted between devices on a network. It acts as an agreement between communicating parties regarding the format, timing, sequencing, and error control of the communication process.

Without a protocol, devices would not understand each other's data, making communication impossible. Common examples include TCP/IP, HTTP, and FTP, which define specific rules for different types of network interactions. …

qs.stem: Which topology requires a multipoint connection?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A bus topology connects devices along one shared backbone, which is a multipoint medium.

Mesh and star generally use point-to-point links.

qs.stem: Select the correct full form of the term ARPANET from the given options.
qs.sol:
Concept

An acronym may be formed from the name of an organization or system. Its expansion must preserve the established words represented by the abbreviated form.

ARPANET combines the agency name ARPA with NET for network, so identifying the historical name behind ARPA determines the expansion.

Application

ARPA was the Advanced Research Projects Agency of the United States Department of Defense. Adding Network to that agency name gives Advanced Research Projects Agency Network.

Contrast

American Research Projects Advance Network substitutes “American” and “Advance” for words in the agency name.

American Research Programs Advance Network also substitutes “Programs” for “Projects”. …

qs.stem: In the context of networking history, what does the first letter ‘A’ stand for in the abbreviation ‘ARPANET’ (developed by the agency ARPA under the U.S. Department of Defense)?
qs.sol: The first letter 'A' in ARPANET stands for 'Advanced', as ARPA was the acronym for the Advanced Research Projects Agency, a U.S. Department of Defense agency that developed ARPANET. This is the correct expansion based on historical records.

qs.stem: Which topology of network is represented in the following diagram ?
qs.sol: The rendered diagram has one central hub and five peripheral nodes. Each peripheral node attaches to the centre by its own spoke, which is star topology.
In a ring topology, each node is connected to exactly two neighboring nodes, forming a closed loop or circular structure.

qs.stem: In which of the topology, each device has a dedicated point-to-point link to a central controller?
qs.sol: Answer:  Star topology

qs.stem: Which type of network shares the communication channel among all the machines?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
In a broadcast network, devices share a common channel and a transmission can be received by all attached machines.

Addressing determines which recipients act on it.

qs.stem: A _____ topology uses a single connection to connect all devices together.
qs.sol: Data compression removes redundant information so that data can be transmitted using less bandwidth and storage space, making communication more efficient.

qs.stem: A _____ topology uses a single connection to connect all devices together.

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Network topology describes the pattern in which devices are connected to each other. Two very different connection patterns are relevant here: a single shared (multipoint) medium, where every device taps into exactly the same physical line at once, and point-to-point links, where each individual connection joins exactly two devices.

A bus topology attaches every device to one common backbone cable. Because that one cable carries the signal for every device, only a single physical connection is needed to link all of them together — which is exactly what the question describes. …

qs.stem:
Which statements are true about Wide Area Network (WAN)?
 I. Covers wide geographical area
 II. Communication takes place by way of satellites, microwaves
 III. Relatively faster than local area network
qs.sol:
Concept

A wide area network connects networks or endpoints across a large geographical region and can operate over media such as leased lines, optical fiber, microwave links, or satellite links. In the usual textbook comparison of LAN and WAN deployments, the WAN’s longer paths and additional intermediate infrastructure often produce higher latency and lower effective speed; individual link speeds can vary.

Application

The coverage statement describes a network spread over a wide geographical area, which is the defining scope of a WAN.

The transmission-media statement names satellite and microwave links, both established long-distance media that can be used for WAN communication. …
Answer:  Servers, clients

qs.stem: ______ is a combination of hardware and software that facilitates the sharing of information between computing devices.
qs.sol: A network is defined as a combination of hardware and software that facilitates the sharing of information between computing devices. This includes components like routers, cables, and communication protocols.

qs.stem: Two devices are in a network if—

opts.A: A process in one device is able to exchange data with a process in another device
opts.B: A process is running on both devices
opts.C: PIDs of the processes running on different devices are same
opts.D:
Both devices have same operating system

E

None of these

qs.sol:
Concept

A computer network exists when distinct devices can communicate and exchange data through a communication medium and agreed protocols. Process execution, local identifiers, or a common operating system alone do not establish that communication relationship.

Application

Identify the entities in the stem: two distinct devices, each capable of hosting processes.

Look for a condition that states communication across the device boundary.

The statement about a process on one device exchanging data with a process on the other directly supplies that condition.

Contrast

Processes merely running on both devices describes local execution, not communication. …

qs.stem: Machine that places the request to access the data is generally called as _____.
qs.sol:
In a client–server architecture, the client machine sends a request to access data or services.
 The server machine receives the request and provides the required data or service.

qs.stem: In the standard Internet architecture classification, which of the following is not an end system at the network edge?
qs.sol:
Concept

In Internet architecture, the network edge consists of end systems, also called hosts, that run application programs. End systems include user devices as well as servers.

Packet-forwarding devices whose main role is to move traffic between links are network infrastructure, not end systems.

Application

A PC and a smartphone are user end systems. A server is also an end system because it hosts network applications and communicates with clients. A switch forwards frames between connected nodes instead of acting as an application host.

Contrast

PC — an end system used to run user applications.

Smartphone — a mobile end system that accesses network services. …

Answer:  LAN (Local Area Network)
 A LAN connects computers and buildings within a limited area such as a campus. CAT6 Ethernet cables are commonly used to build LANs between nearby buildings, which fits the described setup of three close buildings connected by CAT6.
 Why this is a LAN:
 The network covers a small, confined area (the campus).

qs.stem: Which topology of networks is represented in the following diagram?
qs.sol:
Concept

A network topology is the geometric pattern in which nodes and links are arranged. The defining tests are: a bus is one single shared backbone line; a ring is one closed loop; a star is many dedicated links to one central hub; and a tree is a hierarchy in which a root link branches into several lower-level segments — a parent-to-child arrangement, often built by joining bus or star segments through a backbone.

Applying it to this diagram

Start at the short segment on the left; it carries a couple of nodes and acts as the root.

At a junction this root fans out into three separate horizontal segments stacked at one level below it. …

qs.stem: Which one of the following resource is not necessarily required on a file server?
qs.sol:
A file server needs storage, processing and network connectivity to serve files.

A display is optional because it can be administered remotely.

qs.stem: When a collection of various computers appears as a single coherent system to its clients, what is this called?
qs.sol: A distributed system is defined as a collection of autonomous computers that appear to users as a single coherent system. This architecture provides transparency and coherence across multiple nodes, distinguishing it from standard networking where individual systems remain distinct. Therefore, the correct term for this setup is a distributed system.

qs.stem: Here, “terminates the data” means receiving the transfer at its destination. Which choice gives the complete set of the listed computers that can act as nodes in a computer network?

opts.A: The computer that originates the data
opts.B: The computer that routes the data
opts.C: The computer that terminates the data
opts.D:
All of these

E

None of these

qs.sol:
Concept

A network node is any addressable or communicating device that participates in exchanging data over a network.

Nodes may act as end systems that originate or receive data, or as intermediate devices that forward data between network segments.

Application

A source computer originates data and injects it into the network, so it participates as an end node.

A routing computer receives packets and forwards them toward another network, so it participates as an intermediate node.

A destination computer receives the transfer and is the node at which that data communication terminates. …

qs.stem: Which one of the following protocols is not used in internet?
qs.sol:
Correct Answer:
Option E
Concept

A protocol is a standardized set of rules that governs how data is formatted, addressed, transmitted and received between devices. The Internet protocol suite (TCP/IP) is a layered family of such protocols; the application layer in particular hosts many of the protocols that everyday Internet services rely on. To answer a "which one is NOT used" question, you check each candidate against this suite: if it is a recognized, standardized member of the TCP/IP stack, it IS used on the Internet. …

qs.stem: A high-speed communication equipment typically would not be needed for

opts.C: supporting communication between nodes in a LAN
opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
High-speed communication equipment is typically needed where large bandwidth, fast transfer rates, or fast local/network communication are important.

A. E-mail: E-mail is generally a low-bandwidth, asynchronous service. Text mails and ordinary attachments do not normally require high-speed communication equipment.
B. Transferring large volume of data: Large data transfer needs high bandwidth and faster data rates, so high-speed equipment is useful or necessary.
C. Supporting communication between nodes in a LAN: LAN communication is built around network equipment such as switches/NICs and standard fast local links. …

opts.D:

Question not attempted

qs.stem: ISPs exchange internet traffic between their networks at a shared interconnection facility called ______.
qs.sol:
Modified from the original question: the printed Bihar STET item has four choices; this used live record has an additional gateway distractor. The stored option IDs and order are preserved because the question is in a test.

An Internet exchange point is shared switching infrastructure where independently operated networks interconnect and exchange traffic.

A subscriber endpoint serves a customer, an ISP endpoint terminates one provider connection, and a gateway forwards packets; none names the shared facility.
