Answer:  Optical fiber cable (ऑप्टिकल फाइबर केबल)
 Optical fiber transmits information as light signals through a core surrounded by cladding with a lower refractive index.

qs.stem: Which of the following wired medium will be able to have highest speed data communication possible?
qs.sol:
A wired medium's achievable data-communication speed is set mainly by its available bandwidth and by how quickly the carried signal weakens (attenuation) with distance: media that carry information as pulses of light through a glass or plastic fiber support a far larger bandwidth and far lower attenuation than media that carry an electrical signal through a copper conductor.

Among the four options, only fiber optic cable transmits data as light pulses; the remaining three (single pair telephone cable, co-axial cable, twisted pair cable) all carry an electrical signal over copper conductors and are therefore bounded by copper's bandwidth-distance limits. …

qs.stem: The device bridge is used at ____ layer of OSI reference model.
qs.sol: The OSI model classifies each networking device by the layer at which it reads and acts on information. The Physical layer (Layer 1) only regenerates or repeats raw bits, with no awareness of addresses (repeaters, hubs). The Data Link layer (Layer 2) adds hardware (MAC) addressing, so a device here can read a frame's destination address and decide whether to forward or block it (bridges, switches). The Network layer (Layer 3) adds logical (IP) addressing and path selection across different networks (routers). The Transport layer (Layer 4) manages end-to-end delivery between processes (TCP/UDP). The Application layer (Layer 7) defines protocols used directly by user-facing software. …

qs.stem: Bridge works in which layer of the OSI model?
qs.sol:
Answer:  A bridge operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) of the OSI model.
 Why: Bridges forward and filter link-layer frames using MAC addresses; they do not make routing decisions based on IP addresses or examine transport-layer ports.
 Learns MAC addresses and builds a forwarding (MAC) table.

qs.stem: Which network device operates at the Network Layer and makes forwarding decisions based on IP addresses?
qs.sol: The network layer uses logical IP addresses to choose the next hop between networks. A router examines the destination IP address and its routing table before forwarding a packet. Therefore the device described is a router.

qs.stem: Which device is needed to connect two computer systems, if the systems use different protocols ?
qs.sol: A gateway connects networks or systems that use different protocols by translating between them.

qs.stem: Wireless transmission of signals can be done via

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Wireless transmission means sending data without physical cables, using electromagnetic waves. It can be done using multiple types of signals:

Radio waves

Microwaves

Infrared

All three are valid wireless communication methods depending on range, frequency, and application.

A repeater is a network device used to regenerate and strengthen weak signals

It helps in extending the communication distance in a network

Works at the Physical layer (Layer 1) of the OSI model

Ensures that signals do not get degraded over long distances

qs.stem: Which computer hardware device used to convert data from a digital format into a format suitable for an analog transmission medium ? Select the best answer out of the given options.
qs.sol: TPDU represents the data exchanged between transport layer entities, ensuring end-to-end communication between processes on different systems.

qs.stem: Which computer hardware device used to convert data from a digital format into a format suitable for an analog transmission medium ? Select the best answer out of the given options.
qs.sol: A modem modulates digital data into analog signals for transmission and demodulates them back at the receiving end.

A light-based transmission medium is not affected by electromagnetic noise. Light can carry high data rates over long spans, though the installation is comparatively expensive. Those combined features identify optical fiber.

qs.stem: Optical ﬁbre works on the principle of:
qs.sol: At the fibre core-cladding boundary, total internal reflection keeps light inside the core.

The question describes a device that forwards packets between networks using routing information. This functionality is specific to a router, which operates at the network layer to direct traffic based on IP addresses. Therefore, option 2 is the correct answer.

qs.stem: Which device acts as a “traffic controller” to connect two different networks (like your home LAN and the internet) and determines the best path for data packets?
qs.sol: A router is the device responsible for connecting different networks, such as a local area network (LAN) to the internet. It acts as a traffic controller by examining data packets and determining the most efficient path for them to travel between networks.

qs.stem: Which device is used to connect multiple devices within the same local area network (LAN)?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
A LAN switch forwards frames between attached local devices using MAC addresses.

A router chiefly joins different IP networks; a bridge is a limited two-segment device.

The device normally used to connect multiple LAN devices is the switching device.

qs.stem: Which device is used to connect multiple devices within the same local area network (LAN)?
qs.sol: The message is split into smaller units, and each unit carries addressing and ordering information. The receiver uses those numbers to reconstruct the original message. This is how packet switching transmits data.

qs.stem: In a Local Area Network (LAN), a Cat 6 Ethernet cable of approximately 160 meters is used to connect a network device to the server. Due to the excessive length of the cable, signal loss is occurring. Which of the following devices is most suitable to amplify and retransmit the signals between the server and the device?
qs.sol: A long cable attenuates its signal. A repeater regenerates the received physical-layer signal and retransmits it along the link.

qs.stem: In a Local Area Network (LAN), a Cat 6 Ethernet cable of approximately 160 meters is used to connect a network device to the server. Due to the excessive length of the cable, signal loss is occurring. Which of the following devices is most suitable to amplify and retransmit the signals between the server and the device?
qs.sol: Tree topology follows a hierarchical structure with multiple branches and is commonly used to connect several LANs.

qs.stem: Bridges work at which of the following OSI/ISO reference model's layers?
qs.sol:
Concept: The OSI model assigns network functions to layers according to their responsibilities and the information they process.

A layer is identified by its protocol data unit and addressing scope; application dialogue, inter-network routing, and local-link delivery are different responsibilities.

Application: A bridge connects LAN segments and processes frames using link-level destination addresses.

Suppose a frame enters one bridge port with source MAC address S and destination MAC address D. The bridge learns that S is reachable through the incoming port.

The bridge consults its forwarding table for D. …

qs.stem: Which of the following wireless communication media is primarily used by a standard Wi-Fi router for data transmission in a computer network?
qs.sol: A patent requires novelty. Since extant knowledge already exists, it lacks novelty and cannot be patented. Thus, “Extant knowledge is not patentable.”

qs.stem: Which of the following wireless communication media is primarily used by a standard Wi-Fi router for data transmission in a computer network?
qs.sol:
Wi-Fi transfers data using radio-frequency electromagnetic waves, commonly in gigahertz frequency bands.

The other listed wave types are not the usual communication medium of a standard Wi-Fi router.

qs.stem: Frames from one LAN can be transmitted to another LAN via a device called
qs.sol: A bridge is used at the Data Link Layer of the OSI model to connect one network to another. A bridge can connect multiple LAN segments and forward frames between them.

qs.stem: Which device is used to connect multiple devices within the same local area network (LAN)?

opts.D:
More than one of these

E

None of these

qs.sol:
Concept

Networking devices are classified by the OSI layer at which they operate and the scope of connectivity they provide. A switch works at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) and is built with multiple ports specifically to connect many end devices within one LAN, forwarding frames using the MAC address table it builds for each connected device. A router works at the Network Layer (Layer 3) and joins separate networks (for example, a LAN to the internet) using IP addressing. A traditional bridge also works at Layer 2, but its classical role is to join two LAN/Ethernet segments into one, typically over a small number of interfaces — it is not built as a multiport device for many end devices. …

qs.stem: Eila Gulati is planning to connect 25 computers of her training center using Ethernet Cable. Which one of the following devices should she use for the same?
qs.sol: An Ethernet switch connects the computers in one local network and forwards data to the intended port. A unit with enough ports is needed for 25 computers.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a connectivity standard for transferring digital instrument data?
qs.sol: MIDI is the digital protocol for exchanging musical instrument performance messages. The other names denote multimedia control or audio formats.
Optical fiber cable is best suited for connecting offices in different or nearby cities because it supports very high bandwidth, long-distance communication, high speed, and low signal loss.

Correct answer: To provide Internet access to multiple devices by routing traffic between the local network and the Internet.

Explanation:

A router forwards data packets between different networks (for example, between your home network and the Internet).

To allow multiple devices to use one Internet connection, routers commonly use Network Address Translation (NAT) and provide DHCP to assign local IP addresses.

Routers may also include basic security features (firewall rules, access control), but comprehensive network security is usually handled by dedicated security systems. …

qs.stem: Identify the device from the following options that usually links two homogeneous packed broadcast local networks.
qs.sol: A bridge connects two homogeneous LANs (same type of network) and operates at the data link layer. It forwards frames based on MAC addresses and is commonly used to link similar broadcast networks.

qs.stem: Which of the following devices understands the format and contents of the data and translates messages from one format to another?
qs.sol:
Concept: A device's position in the OSI model decides how much of a message it can understand. A device working at the application layer can read the meaning and format of the data itself; devices working at the physical, data-link, or network layers only move bits, frames, or packets without understanding what the payload actually contains.

Application: The question describes exactly this ability — understanding a message's format and translating it into a different format. …

qs.stem: Which wireless communication medium best describes what a standard Wi-Fi router uses for data transmission in a computer network?
qs.sol:
Correct answer: Radio waves (microwave-frequency RF)

Wi-Fi uses radio-frequency electromagnetic waves, commonly in bands such as 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.

These GHz bands are often called microwave bands in electromagnetic-spectrum tables. Microwaves are part of the broader radio-frequency/radio-wave range used for wireless communication.

Since the option list does not separately provide “microwaves,” the best and correct broader category is radio waves.

qs.stem: Network devices ………………… and ………………… are used at physical layer.
qs.sol:
Hub: Essentially a multiport repeater that forwards incoming bit-level signals to all other ports without addressing or frame processing (Layer 1).

Why the other devices are not correct:
 Bridge: Operates at the Data Link layer (Layer 2) and forwards frames based on MAC addresses.

Switch: Operates at the Data Link layer (Layer 2), using MAC addresses to forward frames to the correct port.

Router: Operates at the Network layer (Layer 3) and routes packets between different networks using IP addresses.

Gateway: Typically operates at higher layers (often application layer) performing protocol translation between different network architectures or applications. …

qs.stem: Which of the following devices is essential to set up a wired LAN?
qs.sol: A wired LAN requires devices to have a NIC and Ethernet cables, often connected through switches or hubs for communication within a local network.

qs.stem: Which of the following components cannot be directly connected to a standard USB or HDMI port without the use of an intermediate adapter?
qs.sol: Standard USB and HDMI ports are designed for specific types of connections. USB ports connect devices like keyboards, mice, and storage drives using USB connectors. HDMI ports transmit video and audio signals to displays or projectors. Ethernet cables, however, use RJ45 connectors designed for network ports (LAN). Because the physical connector shapes and signal protocols differ, an Ethernet cable cannot be plugged directly into a USB or HDMI port without an intermediate adapter.

qs.stem: What kind of transmission medium is most appropriate to carry data in a computer network that is exposed to electrical interference?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

A transmission medium carries information either as an electrical signal in a conductor or as light in a dielectric waveguide. Electromagnetic interference can induce unwanted voltage or current only when the data path couples to an external electromagnetic field.

Therefore, immunity to electrical interference depends on the signal mechanism and material of the medium, not merely on its nominal data rate.

Application

Unshielded twisted pair and coaxial cable use copper conductors and electrical signalling. Twisting or shielding reduces coupled noise, but it does not make a conductive data path intrinsically immune to electromagnetic interference. …

qs.stem: Which device is “intelligent” enough to learn the MAC addresses of connected devices and send data only to the specific port of the intended recipient?
qs.sol: The device described is a network switch. Unlike hubs that broadcast data to all ports, switches operate at Layer 2 and learn MAC addresses to forward frames only to the specific port connected to the intended recipient. This intelligent forwarding distinguishes switches from hubs and repeaters.

qs.stem: For packet-mode terminals connected to public data networks, the X.25 standard specifies which of the following?
qs.sol:
Concept: A communication standard may define character framing, an access method, an equipment interface, or a physical transmission rate. The scope is identified from the standard’s formal subject and the layer of communication it governs.

Application: X.25 defines packet-mode operation at the boundary between Data Terminal Equipment (DTE) and Data Circuit-terminating Equipment (DCE). DTE is the subscriber-side terminal or host, while DCE is the network-side equipment that provides access to the packet-switched network.

Technique for start-stop data: this is asynchronous character framing with start and stop bits. …

qs.stem: Name the standards-based, point-to-point, serial interconnect capable of high-bandwidth transfers, used throughout the computing and embedded devices industries, introduced in 2004.
qs.sol: PCI Express uses serial, point-to-point lanes for high-bandwidth peripheral interconnection.

qs.stem: The ____ houses the switches in a Token Ring network.
qs.sol:
Media Access Control (MAC) deals with how multiple devices share and access a communication medium (who gets to transmit and when).

Protocols/technologies used in MAC define access methods like contention or token passing.

qs.stem: The ____ houses the switches in a Token Ring network.

Application

In IBM Token Ring, the multi-station unit that contains these internal switching and bypass functions is the MAU, also called the MSAU (Multistation Access Unit). It joins several stations while maintaining the logical ring.

A transceiver combines transmitting and receiving functions at a physical-medium interface. …

qs.stem: Which one of the following transmission systems provides the highest data rate to an individual device?
qs.sol:
Answer:  The computer bus provides the highest data rate to an individual device.
 Why: Internal computer buses (for example, the memory bus or PCI Express) are designed to move large volumes of data directly between the processor, memory, and peripherals with very high throughput. These internal links operate at much higher effective data rates than typical external communication systems.
 Telephone systems: built for voice/narrowband services, so data rates are low compared with internal bus speeds.

topics.deep:
- **Guided (wired) media:** **Twisted pair** (UTP/STP; carries electrical current; RJ-45 connector; Cat5 100 Mbps, Cat5e/Cat6 1 Gbps, Cat6a/7 10 Gbps; max 100 m), **Coaxial** (copper core, insulator, braided shield; RG ratings RG-6, RG-58, RG-59; 10Base2 thin 'Thinnet' 185 m, 10Base5 thick 500 m; BNC connectors, cable TV), **Optical fibre** (light pulses by total internal reflection; immune to EMI, highest bandwidth, longest distance, most secure, costly, hard to tap; ST/SC/LC connectors).
- **UTP vs STP:** shielding reduces EMI/crosstalk but both attenuate; STP costlier and heavier. Twisting cancels interference. Colour code for RJ-45: straight-through (PC to switch), crossover (PC to PC; like devices).
- **Fibre:** **multimode** (**step-index** and **graded-index** variants, thick core ~50/62.5 µm, LEDs, short distance) and **single-mode** (core ~8–10 µm, laser, long distance, least dispersion). 'Ungraded index' is not a mode. Cladding has lower refractive index than core. Light is generated by LED or ILD, detected by photodiode.
- **Unguided (wireless) media:** carry electromagnetic waves with no conductor. Propagation: **ground (<2 MHz), sky/ionospheric (2–30 MHz), line-of-sight (>30 MHz)**. Bands: radio waves (3 kHz–1 GHz, omnidirectional, penetrate walls), microwaves (1–300 GHz, unidirectional, line of sight, satellite & cellular), infrared (300 GHz–400 THz, short range, cannot pass walls, TV remote), light (laser). Radio waves at low frequency pass obstacles well but power falls off sharply with distance (path loss).
- **Satellite:** uplink (earth -> satellite), downlink (satellite -> earth); transponder shifts frequency. GEO 36,000 km (~0.25 s delay), MEO, LEO (Iridium, Starlink).
- **Network devices and OSI layer:**
| Device | OSI layer | Function |
|---|---|---|
| Repeater/Hub (multiport repeater) | 1 Physical | regenerate signal; hub has one collision domain |
| Bridge / Switch | 2 Data Link | filter by MAC; switch = multiport bridge, each port own collision domain |
| Router | 3 Network | connects networks, forwards by IP, separates broadcast domains |
| Gateway | up to 7 (protocol translator) | connects dissimilar networks/protocols |
| Modem | 1 | modulate/demodulate |
| Access point | 2 | wireless to wired bridge |
- **Router** in TCP/IP model operates at the **Internet layer** (OSI network layer). Router has **filtering and forwarding** (routing table, ACLs); it is not an amplifier; it connects different networks, not just segments of one; it forwards packets. A **layer-3 switch** routes too. **Brouter** = bridge + router. **Repeater** amplifies/regenerates; **amplifier** boosts analog signals including noise.
- **Collision vs broadcast domains:** hub: 1 collision domain, 1 broadcast domain. Switch: n collision domains, 1 broadcast domain (without VLAN). Router: each interface separate broadcast and collision domain.
- **Ethernet cabling names:** 10Base-T (UTP, 100 m), 100Base-TX, 100Base-FX (fibre), 1000Base-T, 10GBase-SR. Meaning: speed Mbps, Base = baseband, T = twisted pair.
- **Connectors:** RJ-45 (UTP), RJ-11 (telephone), BNC (coax), SC/ST/LC (fibre), SFP (transceiver). 'RJ55', 'RS45' are fake.
- **Common traps:** infrared is unguided; coaxial is guided; twisted pair carries electric current not light; STP still suffers attenuation; gateway 'works at Transport layer' in some matching items but really any layer/up to application; hub is physical-layer not data link.
- **Likely question angles:** (1) max segment lengths of Thinnet/Thicknet/UTP; (2) number of collision domains in a switch network; (3) fibre type for long-haul and its source; (4) crossover vs straight cable use; (5) match devices with layer; (6) why fibre is immune to EMI; (7) wireless propagation modes and frequencies; (8) device that separates broadcast domains; (9) GEO satellite delay; (10) categories of UTP and speeds.

topics.unit: Unit 2 · Reference Models & Data Link Layer
topics.title: 5. OSI & TCP/IP Reference Models
topics.theory:
- **OSI layers (7→1):** Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical (mnemonic *All People Seem To Need Data Processing*). Layer 5 = Session.
- **Physical:** bits, signals, media · **Data link:** framing, MAC/physical addressing, error & flow control, access control, node-to-node delivery · **Network:** logical (IP) addressing, **routing**, path selection, host-to-host across networks · **Transport:** process-to-process, segmentation, reliability, ports · **Session:** **dialog control, token management, synchronisation/checkpoints** · **Presentation:** translation, encryption, compression · **Application:** user services.
- Layers 1–3 are **hop-by-hop**; layers 4–7 are **end-to-end**.
- The *routing algorithm* decides the output line for an incoming packet — part of network-layer software.
- **TCP/IP 4 layers:** Application, Transport, Internet, Network-access (host-to-network).

qs.stem: In OSI model network layer is responsible for __________.
qs.sol: The Network layer (Layer 3) is responsible for routing packets from source to destination using logical addressing (IP).
qs.rel: Network layer: logical (IP) addressing, routing, fragmentation, congestion control; PDU = packet. Dialog control/token management is session layer; physical transmission is layer 1; framing/MAC is layer 2.

qs.stem: Which of the following devices works at the network layer of the ISO-OSI reference model?
qs.sol: Concept: in the ISO-OSI model a device belongs to the highest layer whose information it actually interprets. A physical-layer (Layer 1) device handles only the raw signal or bit stream and reads no address at all; a data-link-layer (Layer 2) device interprets MAC frame headers inside one network; a network-layer (Layer 3) device interprets logical (IP) addresses and forwards packets between separate networks along a path it chooses. …
qs.rel: Router = network layer (L3); hub/repeater = L1; bridge/switch = L2. Router forwards IP packets between networks. Amplifier is an analog boosting device. Layer-3 switch combines both.

qs.stem: Which layer in OSI model is responsible for the dialogue control and token management?
qs.sol:
Session layer (सेशन लेयर) is Responsible for dialogue control (who speaks when)

Handles token management to avoid data collision.
qs.rel: Session layer (5): dialog control (half/full duplex), token management, synchronisation/checkpoints. Presentation layer: encryption, compression, translation. Transport: end-to-end reliability, port addressing.

qs.stem: Layer five of OSI model is ______.
qs.sol:
In the OSI model, numbering starts from the bottom: layer 1 is Physical, layer 2 is Data Link, layer 3 is Network, layer 4 is Transport, layer 5 is Session, layer 6 is Presentation, and layer 7 is Application.

Therefore, layer 5 is the Session layer. Layer 3 is the Network layer, so the reported statement confuses layer 3 with layer 5.
qs.rel: OSI order from bottom: Physical 1, Data Link 2, Network 3, Transport 4, Session 5, Presentation 6, Application 7. PDUs: bits, frames, packets, segments. TCP/IP merges 5-7 into Application.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a part of the network layer software in OSI model responsible for deciding which output line an incoming packet should be transmitted on?
qs.sol:
The network layer must choose an outgoing link for each packet.

A routing algorithm determines that forwarding path or output line.
qs.rel: Routing algorithm lives in network layer; it decides the outgoing line (routing table/forwarding). Types: adaptive (distance vector, link state) vs non-adaptive (static, flooding). MAC protocols and framing belong to the data link layer.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true regarding OSI layers in computer networks?
 Statements:
 I. The session layer provides means of establishing, maintaining and terminating a session between two end users.
 II. Data Link layer sets up a logical path between the source and destination computer of the network.
qs.sol:
The primary role of the Session Layer (Layer 5) is "dialogue control." It manages the communication session between applications. It handles synchronization (checkpoints) so that if a connection drops, the data transfer can resume from the last known good point rather than starting over. 

The Data Link Layer (Layer 2) is responsible for "node-to-node" delivery (moving data between two physically connected devices, like our laptop and our router). The Network Layer is what handles "end-to-end" logical paths across multiple different networks using IP addressing.
qs.rel: Session layer establishes, maintains, terminates sessions and sets checkpoints; the data link layer gives node-to-node delivery (framing, MAC, error control) while the network layer sets up logical source-destination paths.

qs.stem:
Which statement is/are true about the OSI model?

I. Layer 1 through 3 are end-to-end 

II. Layer 4 through 7 are chained
qs.sol:
❌ Statement I: “Layer 1 through 3 are end-to-end”

This is false.

Layers 1–3 (Physical, Data Link, Network) are hop-by-hop, not end-to-end.

They handle transmission between adjacent devices (like routers).

End-to-end communication is mainly handled by higher layers (especially Layer 4).

❌ Statement II: “Layer 4 through 7 are chained”

This is also false.

Layers 4–7 (Transport, Session, Presentation, Application) are actually end-to-end layers, not “chained.”

The term “chained” is not a standard or correct description in the OSI model context.
qs.rel: Layers 1-3 operate hop-by-hop; layers 4-7 are end-to-end (transport onward run only on end hosts). Intermediate routers implement only layers 1-3. Don't confuse with 'chained'.

qs.sol:
The OSI reference model names the Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation and Application layers.

Counting these distinct layers gives seven.

qs.stem: The number of layers in ISO-OSI reference model is —
qs.sol:
The OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) model consists of 7 layers:
 Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

qs.stem: OSI stands for:
qs.sol: The reference model names a framework for interconnecting open computer systems in layers.

Routing is performed by the Network Layer in the OSI model. The Network Layer is responsible for determining the best path (routing) for data packets to travel from the source host to the destination host across different networks.

qs.stem: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for logical addressing and routing packets between networks ?

opts.D:
Session Layer

E

Question not attempted

qs.sol:
Concept: The OSI model assigns different jobs to layers. A logical network address identifies a destination beyond a single local link; routing selects the path or next hop for a packet between networks.

Application: Consider a computer sending data to a server on another network.

The data-link layer places the packet in a frame for delivery over the current link.

The network layer reads the destination logical address and a router chooses the next hop toward the destination network.

At each later link the frame can change, while the packet is forwarded toward its destination. …

qs.stem: Which protocol layer uses the protocol SMTP, HTTP, FTP?
qs.sol:
Answer: Application layer

Explanation: SMTP, HTTP, and FTP are protocols that define how applications communicate and exchange data. They operate at the application layer of the networking stack.

SMTP: used for sending and routing email between mail servers and clients.

HTTP: used for transferring web pages and resources between web servers and browsers.

FTP: used for transferring files between hosts over a network.

Additional note: These application protocols typically rely on transport-layer protocols (for example, TCP) to provide reliable data delivery. …

Encryption and Decryption is the responsibility of the Presentation layer.
 Explanation:
 The Presentation layer is responsible for data formatting, compression, and encryption. It ensures that data sent from the application layer is in a format that can be read by the receiving application. This includes converting data into a common format and securing it through encryption before transmission.
 The Physical layer handles the transmission of raw bits over a medium and does not manage encryption. The Application layer provides user interfaces and network services but does not handle encryption directly. The Network layer manages routing and logical addressing, not data security. …

Concept: Network communication uses a different identifier at each layer. An IP address routes a packet toward a host interface, while a transport protocol uses a port number to select an endpoint within that host.

Application: The question asks for the transport-layer identifier, so the relevant term is port number. The printed choice ‘Port Numbe’ is a truncated rendering of that term.

Contrast with the other identifiers:

Subnet Mask divides the network and host portions of an IP address.

MAC Address identifies an interface for delivery on the local link.

IP Address identifies a network-layer destination for packet routing. …

qs.stem: In the OSI model, end-to-end host-to-host connectivity is provided by the:
qs.sol:
The Data Link Layer is divided into two sublayers:

Logical Link Control (LLC)

Media Access Control (MAC)

 Key idea

The sublayer that depends on the type of transmission medium (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, etc.) is the MAC sublayer.

It handles:

Access to physical medium

Frame transmission rules

Hardware addressing (MAC address)

It varies based on the medium used (wired vs wireless)

qs.stem: In the OSI model, end-to-end host-to-host connectivity is provided by the:

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept

A layer provides a service to the layer above it and uses the service below it. Providing a communication service is different from merely operating at the communicating endpoints.

The OSI transport service transfers data between transport-service users, shielding upper layers from the details of the underlying network service. Higher-layer dialogue management is a separate function.

Application

Consider an application on one computer sending data to an application on another. The transport layer accepts data from its service user and, where needed, segments it for transmission.

The network layer carries packets across the intervening networks using addressing and routing. …

qs.stem: Which layer of the TCP/IP stack corresponds to the OSI model transport layer?

opts.D:
More than one of the above

E

None of the above

qs.sol:
Concept: A protocol layer is identified by the service it provides to the layer above, rather than by its name alone.

Layer correspondence compares service boundaries: application semantics, end-to-end delivery between processes, and routing between networks are distinct responsibilities.

Application: The OSI transport layer provides end-to-end process communication. In the four-layer TCP/IP model, this service belongs to the transport layer, also called the host-to-host layer.

Consider a web browser sending data to a server. The application protocol specifies the meaning of the request. …

qs.stem: X.21 is

opts.A: a method of determining which device has access to the transmission medium at any time
opts.B: a media access control technique for multiple-access transmission media
opts.C: a very common link-oriented protocol issued by ISO
opts.D: a network access standard for connecting stations to a circuit switch network

qs.sol:
Concept: X.21 is an ITU-T (formerly CCITT) recommendation that defines the electrical and functional interface between Data Terminal Equipment (DTE) and Data Circuit-terminating Equipment (DCE) for synchronous operation on public data networks -- in short, a network access standard that lets a station attach to and be recognized by a circuit-switched data network.

Application: Among the four descriptions offered, only one matches this definition: a network access standard for connecting stations to a circuit switch network precisely restates what X.21 does -- it is the DTE-DCE interface standard used to attach a station to a circuit-switched network. …

qs.stem: X.21 is
qs.sol: The point where a secure internal network meets an untrusted external network, with a firewall installed, is known as a chokepoint. A chokepoint is a strategic location where all traffic must pass through, allowing for monitoring and control. Firewalls are placed at chokepoints to filter and secure data flow between networks. This makes 'Chokepoint' the correct term for this scenario.
In OSI model physical, Datalink and network layer are hop-to-hop layer when Transport, Session, Presentation and Application layer are end-to-end or host-to-host layer.

qs.stem: Which of the following is false with regard to ISO/OSI reference layer?

opts.A: Presentation Layer deals with data encryption
opts.B: Physical Layer is handles transmission of raw bits over the communication channel
opts.C: Transport Layer provides token management service
opts.D: The task of flow control is done by data link layer

qs.sol: In the OSI model, token management is a function of the Session Layer. The Presentation Layer handles encryption, the Physical Layer transmits raw bits, and the Data Link Layer performs flow control. Hence, the statement that the Transport Layer provides token management service is false.

qs.stem: X.21 is

opts.A: a method of determining which device has access to the transmission medium at any time
opts.B: a method access control technique for multiple access transmission media
opts.C: very common but oriented at linked protocol issued to ISO
opts.D: a network access standard for connecting stations to a circuit switch network

Primarily describes the DTE–DCE interface used for synchronous digital connections to circuit‑switched telecommunication networks.

Specifies connector pinouts and signaling conventions used to interconnect equipment and the network.
